25 December – Kolyada Festival (wheel of fortune, beginning of the 
new sun) – New Year.
1–5 January – Christmas holidays.
1 March (14 March according to the new calendar) – first day of spring 
– Evdokiev Day.
21 March – Maslenitsa – a whole week during the spring equinox, a 
holiday to see off winter and welcome spring.
Early June – Trinity Sunday – honoring of ancestors.
Early June – Semik (zelena nedilya for Ukrainians) – a holiday for 
girls, dancing around birch trees. A display of brides.
6–7 July – Summer solstice holiday. Sacred fires are lit, and 
participants in the ritual jump over them: the ritual is intended to ensure 
fertility (the height of the jump determines the height of the grain, etc.).
Bathing rituals are associated with fire and water and serve as a 
celebration of pairing, when young men and women found their beloved.
The end of July is the festival of Perun. The festival instilled a warrior 
spirit in men.
21 September is Ovsyen, the festival of the autumn equinox. It marks 
the end of summer.
24 September – Kapusta Barynya – youth gatherings, cabbage parties.
